title: Instagrammable Bhutan | Couple Special
highlights: Explore Bhutan with a romantic escape through scenic valleys, ancient monasteries, and the serene beauty of the Himalayas.
Discover serenity beneath the majestic 177-foot Buddha Dordenma in Thimphu, an impressive statue that houses 125,000 smaller Buddhas within.
Visit Motithang Takin Preserve in Thimphu, home to Bhutan's national animal, the takin and enjoy close encounters with these unique creatures.
Trek to Tiger’s Nest, a monastery perched at 3,120 meters on a cliff, where the spirit of Guru Rinpoche's meditations remains.
Witness the grandeur of Rinpung Dzong, a stunning fortress-monastery in Bhutan, known for its impressive architecture and rich history,
inclusions: 1 night stay in Phuntsholing with breakfast and lunch or dinner
2 nights stay in Thimphu City with breakfast and lunch or dinner

2 nights stay in Paro with breakfast and lunch or dinner

know_before_you_go: Cancellation After Rescheduling: Clients who reschedule their tours or treks but later decide to cancel will be subject to our standard cancellation policy. Any rescheduling fees paid will be non-refundable.
Images are for representation purpose only.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: Welcome to Siliguri! Upon your arrival at Siliguri Railway Station or Bagdogra Airport, get driven to your hotel in Phuntsholing. Check in and spend your time at leisure. You can visit the beautifully detailed Bhutan Gate, or head to Zangto Pelri to admire the impressive statues of Guru Padmasambhava. You can also explore Karbandi Monastery, one of the oldest Monasteries in Bhutan. Afterward, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
days.desc: In the morning, check out from your hotel and visit the immigration office to get your travel permit. Then, get driven to your hotel in Thimphu. Check in and spend the day exploring the city at your leisure. You can stroll through Clock Tower Square to admire stunning Bhutanese architecture, or dive into the nation's history at Simply Bhutan. If you love nature, the Royal Botanical Garden is a must-see for its diverse plant life. Afterward, return to your hotel for a relaxing overnight stay.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, get transferred for a sightseeing tour of Thimphu. First, visit the National Memorial Chorten, a stupa remembering Bhutan's third king. Next, stop by the Motithang Takin Preserve to catch a glimpse of the national animal. Then, enjoy some shopping at the bustling Handicrafts Market, and explore the impressive Tashichho Dzong, a fortress-monastery with stunning architecture and sacred temples. After your exploration, you’ll be driven back to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Paro | Leisure Day
days.desc: After checking out from the hotel, get driven to Paro. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and spend your time at leisure. You can visit Zuri Dzong Fort, where you can wander along its ancient paths and take in breathtaking views of the Paro Valley. You can also stroll along the banks of the Paro Chu River, or, for a touch of adventure, trek to the sacred cliffside site of Drakarpo. Afterward, return to the hotel for a comfortable overnight stay.

days.title: Hike to Tiger's Nest Monastery
days.desc: Today, get driven to Ta Dzong, a historic watchtower transformed into a national museum. Afterward, visit the grand Rinpung Dzong, an architectural marvel. Then, get transferred to Tiger’s Nest and embark on your hike to the iconic Taktsang Monastery. As you ascend, the trail leads you through pine forests covered in colorful prayer flags. Inside the monastery, you'll be greeted by intricate prayer wheels and murals honoring Guru Rinpoche. Conclude your day with getting driven back to the hotel.

days.desc: Today, check out from your hotel and get driven to Phuntsholing. En route, make a stop at the breathtaking Chele La Pass. Upon arrival in Phuntsholing, get driven to your hotel. Check in and spend your time at leisure. You can wander to Alapan’s View Point for stunning views, or marvel at the impressive Chukha Hydropower Dam. You can also visit Gumpha Mandir, known for its intricate Tibetan architecture. Afterward, return to your hotel for a relaxing overnight stay.
